studies.name: INTerpath-001 (Phase 3, NCT05933577) — 19 August 2026 topline press release
studies.draft_uses: Topline announcement only: RFS and DMFS endpoints met, 'statistically significant and clinically meaningful'; no hazard ratio, no confidence interval, no p-value, no percentage released. Trial design figures: 1,137 patients, 2:1 randomisation, double-blind, stage IIB–IV, investigator-assessed RFS, estimated primary completion 26 October 2029.
studies.latest_known: Same 19 August 2026 Merck/Moderna press release remains the only data release as of 2 September 2026. No hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values or event-rate percentages have been published. The companies state data 'will be presented at an upcoming international medical meeting and shared with regulatory authorities.' NCT05933577 registry record carries no posted results and was last updated 24 September 2025 (still lists 1,089 estimated enrolment, not the announced 1,137). Confirmed as of 2 September 2026.
studies.what_changed: No efficacy figures have been released at any readout; the draft correctly reports this absence. Nothing to supersede.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 / mRNA-4157-P201 — 5-year update (ASCO 2026 abstract + JCO full paper, 1 June 2026)
studies.draft_uses: RFS HR 0.510 (95% CI 0.294–0.887); DMFS HR 0.411 (95% CI 0.200–0.843); OS HR 0.471 (95% CI 0.165–1.345) exploratory, n=14 deaths (7 per arm); 4-year RFS rates 72.4% (62.2–80.2) vs 49.1% (33.3–63.0); OS survival rates 92.2% (84.2–96.3) vs 85.6% (70.5–93.3); median follow-up 60.3 months; data cutoff 15 December 2025; five-year analyses described as descriptive.
studies.latest_known: This IS the latest readout, published simultaneously as an ASCO 2026 abstract (JCO 44, suppl 16, abstract 9500; doi:10.1200/JCO.2026.44.16_suppl.9500) and as a full JCO paper (JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026). The RFS and DMFS hazard ratios and the OS hazard ratio in the draft match the press release and the ASCO abstract. HOWEVER: a figure-level conflict exists between the ASCO abstract and the draft's corrected body text for the pembrolizumab-alone arm 5-year OS rate. The ASCO abstract (suppl 9500) gives this as 71.3% (95% CI 35.4–89.6). The draft's corrected body text gives 85.6% (95% CI 70.5–93.3), which it attributes to the JCO full paper (JCO-26-00835). The draft's own 2 September update log explicitly documents this correction, stating it changed from 71.3%/35.4–89.6 to 85.6%/70.5–93.3 and that '71.3 is in the paper once, as the lower bound of a different curve.' Full-text access to JCO-26-00835 is paywalled and the specific figure cannot be independently confirmed from available search results. The conflict between the abstract's 71.3% (35.4–89.6) and the draft's corrected 85.6% (70.5–93.3) for the same arm at the same timepoint is unresolved from external sources.
studies.what_changed: The draft's corrected body text gives the pembrolizumab-alone 5-year OS rate as 85.6% (95% CI 70.5–93.3). The ASCO 2026 abstract from the same data presentation gives 71.3% (95% CI 35.4–89.6) for the same arm. These are materially different figures (85.6% vs 71.3%; CI 70.5–93.3 vs 35.4–89.6). The draft's update log states it corrected to the JCO paper's figure, but the abstract — a citable document from the same readout — gives the lower figure. One of the two figures the draft prints for this endpoint is wrong. The draft cannot be confirmed CURRENT on this specific number without full-text verification of JCO-26-00835. All other figures cited from this readout (RFS HR 0.510 / 0.294–0.887; DMFS HR 0.411 / 0.200–0.843; OS HR 0.471 / 0.165–1.345; combination-arm OS 92.2% / 84.2–96.3; 4-year RFS rates 72.4% / 49.1%) are consistent with the press release and abstract.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — 3-year update (JCO Oncology Advances, DOI 10.1200/OA-25-00008, 2026)
studies.draft_uses: RFS HR 0.510 (95% CI 0.288–0.906) at three years; 80% CI 0.351–0.743 in text; analyses described as 'not intended for formal hypothesis testing (ie, are descriptive only)'; one-sided alpha of 0.10 prespecified; used to establish that the recurrence interval cleared the no-effect line by year three, not year five.
studies.latest_known: The 5-year update (JCO-26-00835, 1 June 2026) is the most recent readout of KEYNOTE-942 efficacy data. The 3-year paper (OA-25-00008) is not superseded for the specific purpose the draft uses it — establishing the year-three interval and the descriptive-only label — because those are facts about the three-year analysis, not claims about the current state of the trial. The draft correctly uses the 3-year paper for the 3-year interval (0.288–0.906) and the 5-year paper for the 5-year interval (0.294–0.887), and explicitly notes the difference. No newer version of the 3-year paper exists.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. The draft uses this paper correctly and for the right timepoint.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — primary Lancet publication (Lancet 403:632–644, February 2024)
studies.draft_uses: RFS HR 0.561 (95% CI 0.309–1.017); two-sided p=0.053; grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events 25% (combination) vs 18% (monotherapy); open-label design; stage IIIB–IV enrolment; arm sizes 107 vs 50; statement that the prespecified analysis was one-sided.
studies.latest_known: This is the primary peer-reviewed publication of the KEYNOTE-942 primary analysis. It has not been corrected, retracted, or superseded by a newer version of the same analysis. The 3-year and 5-year updates are follow-up analyses, not replacements of the primary publication. The figures the draft draws from this paper (HR 0.561, CI 0.309–1.017, p=0.053, AE rates 25%/18%) are the correct primary-analysis figures and are confirmed by the Lancet abstract and the UPenn PDF of the paper. The irAE figure in the Lancet paper is 36% (combination) vs 37% (monotherapy) for immune-mediated AEs — the draft's 'Established' section gives any-grade irAEs as 45.2% vs 44%, which it attributes to the 5-year data, not the Lancet paper. No conflict on figures drawn from the Lancet paper.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. All draft figures attributed to this paper are confirmed against the Lancet abstract and available full text.

studies.name: KEYNOTE-942 — April 2023 company press release (Merck/Moderna, 16 April 2023)
studies.draft_uses: One-sided p=0.0266 for the primary RFS analysis at the initial readout.
studies.latest_known: This is a company press release figure, not a journal publication. The same data were subsequently published in The Lancet (2024) with two-sided p=0.053. The draft correctly notes both figures and explains the one-sided vs two-sided distinction. No newer version of this press release exists; the figure is a historical company-reported value and is not superseded.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. The draft correctly attributes this figure to the company release and distinguishes it from the Lancet's two-sided p=0.053.

studies.name: NCT05933577 — ClinicalTrials.gov registry record for INTerpath-001
studies.draft_uses: Estimated primary completion date 26 October 2029; no posted results as of 2 September 2026; last registry update cited as September 24, 2025.
studies.latest_known: Multiple sources confirm the registry record was last updated 24 September 2025 and still lists 1,089 estimated enrolment (not the announced 1,137). No results have been posted. The draft's statement that the registry 'carries no posted results' and gives an estimated primary completion of 26 October 2029 is confirmed as of 2 September 2026.
studies.what_changed: No figures changed. The registry has not been updated since September 2025 and carries no results.

objections.objection: The draft attributes specific enumerated omissions to MLQ News but MLQ News does not appear in any verifiable source, making the characterisation of their coverage unverifiable.
objections.quote: MLQ News enumerated what was missing: hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, median follow-up, event counts.
objections.why: This is a specific factual claim about a named outlet's editorial conduct — that it listed five specific missing data items. MLQ News does not appear in any search result or in the draft's source list. If the outlet did not enumerate all five items, or if the outlet does not exist under that name, the sentence is wrong and attributes conduct to a third party without evidence. A wronged outlet would be right to object.
objections.fix: Either add MLQ News to the source list with a link to the specific article, quote the enumeration directly, or remove the attribution and describe the enumeration without naming the outlet.

objections.objection: The draft says 'A week on, no numbers have been released' but the piece was updated on 2 September, two weeks after the 19 August announcement.
objections.quote: A week on, no numbers have been released.
objections.why: The original publication was 26 August (one week after the announcement), so 'a week on' was accurate at first publication. After the 2 September update, the same sentence now reads as if only one week has elapsed when it has been two. A reader arriving on 2 September is misled about the timeline.
objections.fix: Change to 'As of this update, no numbers have been released' or 'Two weeks on, no numbers have been released' and update as needed.

objections.objection: The draft makes a significant factual claim about adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors and overall survival without citing any source.
objections.quote: For adjuvant PD-1 inhibitors specifically — the comparison arm in this very trial — no randomised trial against placebo has reported a statistically significant overall survival benefit as a prespecified endpoint in its own population, though indirect comparisons have suggested a signal.
objections.why: This is a sweeping claim about the entire adjuvant PD-1 inhibitor evidence base. It is presented as established fact, but no source is cited for it anywhere in the piece or source list. If it is wrong — if any such trial has reported a prespecified OS benefit — the piece has made a false factual claim in a clinical context where it matters. The absence of a citation is the problem, not necessarily the claim itself.
objections.fix: Add a citation to a systematic review, meta-analysis, or the specific trial records that support this claim, or qualify it as the authors' reading of the literature with a note that readers should verify.

objections.objection: The draft characterises FierceBiotech as having attributed the figures correctly, but provides no link, quote or date for FierceBiotech's coverage.
objections.quote: The outlets we reached attributed those figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — among them The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, OncLive and FierceBiotech
objections.why: The ASCO Post and OncLive coverage is verifiable from search results and consistent with the characterisation. FierceBiotech is named but does not appear in the source list and cannot be verified. Naming an outlet as having done something correctly is still a claim about their conduct; if FierceBiotech's article did not attribute correctly, the sentence is wrong.
objections.fix: Add FierceBiotech to the source list with a link, or remove it from the named list and keep the characterisation general.

objections.objection: The draft characterises Dermatology Times as having stated that 'detailed Phase 3 efficacy metrics were not disclosed,' but Dermatology Times does not appear in the source list and the specific quote cannot be verified.
objections.quote: Dermatology Times that detailed Phase 3 efficacy metrics were not disclosed.
objections.why: This is a specific claim about what a named outlet wrote. Dermatology Times is named in the body but does not appear in the source list. If the outlet did not use that characterisation, the attribution is wrong. A named outlet that did not write what is attributed to it would be right to object.
objections.fix: Add Dermatology Times to the source list with a link and the specific passage, or remove the named attribution and describe the point without naming the outlet.

objections.objection: The draft says 'blinded against the assessment bias the earlier one carried,' implying the Phase 3 is fully protected against that bias, when the draft's own body immediately notes the Phase 3's primary endpoint is investigator-assessed.
objections.quote: It is the more trustworthy trial by a wide margin — seven times larger, and blinded against the assessment bias the earlier one carried.
objections.why: The phrase 'blinded against the assessment bias' implies the bias is eliminated. The very next paragraph explains that the Phase 3's primary endpoint is 'assessed by the investigator' and that an independent review committee would be needed to remove clinical judgement from the endpoint. The sentence is not false — blinding substantially reduces the bias — but 'blinded against' implies a completeness the draft itself qualifies. This is the same issue the correction log says was fixed by removing 'exactly,' but the residual phrasing still overstates.
objections.fix: Change to 'blinded against most of the assessment bias the earlier one carried' or 'substantially protected against the assessment bias the earlier one carried,' consistent with the qualification in the paragraph that follows.

objections.objection: The draft says 'Neither reading reached the general coverage' about the Morning Glory Sciences and Pharmacy Times arguments on stage IIB/IIC risk, but offers no evidence that general coverage was checked for this point.
objections.quote: Neither reading reached the general coverage.
objections.why: This is a claim about what general coverage did not contain — a claim about omission across an unspecified set of outlets. The draft does not say which general outlets were checked or how many. 'Nobody reported X' is a claim about behaviour that requires instances. If any general outlet did cover this point, the sentence is wrong.
objections.fix: Change to 'Neither reading appeared in the general coverage we reviewed' and specify which general outlets were checked, or remove the claim about general coverage entirely.

objections.objection: The draft describes the April 2023 source of the one-sided p-value as a 'press release' in the body but the source list calls it 'first detailed KEYNOTE-942 results,' which was an AACR conference presentation, not a press release.
objections.quote: The April 2023 press release reported KEYNOTE-942 as one-sided p = 0.0266.
objections.why: The AACR 2023 abstract (CT001) is the primary source for the one-sided p = 0.0266 and was a conference presentation, not a press release. The source list labels it 'first detailed KEYNOTE-942 results' without calling it a press release. Calling it a press release in the body mischaracterises the document type, which matters in a piece about the difference between press releases and peer-reviewed data.
objections.fix: Change 'The April 2023 press release' to 'The April 2023 AACR presentation' or 'The April 2023 company announcement' to match the source list and the actual document type.

objections.objection: The draft attributes a specific argument to Morning Glory Sciences — including a direct quote — but Morning Glory Sciences does not appear in the source list and cannot be verified from any search result.
objections.quote: Morning Glory Sciences: the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV, the Phase 3 adds node-negative disease, and 'absolute recurrence risk in that group is lower, so the same hazard ratio delivers a smaller absolute benefit.'
objections.why: A direct quote is attributed to a named outlet. Morning Glory Sciences appears in the body's source attribution but not in the formal source list, and returns no results in search. If the outlet did not publish this argument in these words, the attribution is wrong. A direct quote attributed to a named outlet that did not write it is a correction-level error.
objections.fix: Add Morning Glory Sciences to the source list with a URL and confirm the quote against the original article, or remove the quotation marks and paraphrase with a note that the source is held.

inferences.quote: the Phase 3 enrolled stage IIB–IV, widening it at both ends — down into IIB and IIC, and into IIIA, none of which the earlier trial included
inferences.problem: The expansion was only downward: KEYNOTE-942 already enrolled stage IV, so the upper end did not change; IIB, IIC, and IIIA are all lower-risk stages added below the earlier trial's floor of IIIB.
inferences.correct_reading: INTerpath-001 widened the population downward only, adding stage IIB, IIC, and IIIA below KEYNOTE-942's lower boundary of IIIB; the upper boundary (stage IV) was unchanged.
inferences.fix: the Phase 3 enrolled stage IIB–IV, widening it downward — adding IIB, IIC, and IIIA below the earlier trial's floor of IIIB; the upper boundary, stage IV, was already included

inferences.quote: The confidence interval is the tell: 0.309–1.017 crosses 1.0, which is exactly what a two-sided test keys on.
inferences.problem: The sentence is correct for a two-sided 95% CI / alpha=0.05 framework, but it omits that the prespecified one-sided 90% CI (corresponding to the trial's registered one-sided alpha=0.10) would not cross 1.0 — leaving the reader to infer that the CI crossing 1.0 is a neutral, framework-independent fact, when it is only a feature of the two-sided framing the draft is critiquing.
inferences.correct_reading: The 95% CI crossing 1.0 is consistent with the two-sided p=0.053 exceeding 0.05; under the prespecified one-sided framework at alpha=0.10, the corresponding 90% CI would not cross 1.0, which is why the trial's own threshold was met.
inferences.fix: The confidence interval is the tell: 0.309–1.017 crosses 1.0, which is exactly what a two-sided 95% CI keys on — but the same data, read against the prespecified one-sided 90% CI, would not cross it.

inferences.quote: The source of the one-sided p = 0.0266, which is a company figure and not a journal one.
inferences.problem: The one-sided p = 0.0266 also appears in the ASCO 2023 conference abstract (ASCO abstract LBA9503), which is a peer-reviewed publication, not only in the company press release; characterising it as purely a company figure overstates the distinction.
inferences.correct_reading: The one-sided p = 0.0266 appears in both the April 2023 company press release and the ASCO 2023 conference abstract; the Lancet peer-reviewed paper is the source that switched to two-sided p = 0.053.
inferences.fix: The source of the one-sided p = 0.0266 — a figure that appears in the company release and the ASCO conference abstract, but not in the peer-reviewed Lancet publication, which reported two-sided p = 0.053 instead.

contradictions.quote: MLQ News enumerated what was missing: hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, median follow-up, event counts.
contradictions.counterexample: No MLQ News article appeared in any search result for this story. The outlet that most completely enumerated what was missing — 'hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates' — was Practical Dermatology, which the draft credits only with saying the companies 'had not disclosed Phase 3 efficacy estimates.' The full enumeration the draft attributes to MLQ News is in fact Practical Dermatology's language.
contradictions.fix: Replace 'MLQ News enumerated what was missing: hazard ratios, confidence intervals, p-values, median follow-up, event counts' with 'Practical Dermatology enumerated what was missing: hazard ratios, absolute event rates, and P values.' Remove the claim about median follow-up and event counts unless a source for those specific items can be identified.

contradictions.quote: Most specialist outlets attributed the earlier trial's figures correctly to KEYNOTE-942 — among them The ASCO Post, Dermatology Times, OncLive and FierceBiotech — and several said plainly that no Phase 3 efficacy numbers had been released.
contradictions.counterexample: The attribution finding is correct and if anything understated: Targeted Oncology, CancerNetwork, Biotech Blueprint, Life Science Daily News, KOL Pulse, OncoDaily, EMJ Reviews, Pharmacally, and BioPharm International also correctly attributed the figures to KEYNOTE-942. However, FierceBiotech does not appear in any search result for this story and cannot be confirmed as having covered it at all. The draft should not list FierceBiotech as a confirmed example without a verifiable source.
contradictions.fix: Remove FierceBiotech from the named list unless the article can be located and verified. The broader claim that most specialist outlets attributed figures correctly is well-supported and can be strengthened by adding Targeted Oncology, CancerNetwork, Life Science Daily News, and KOL Pulse to the examples.

contradictions.quote: Practical Dermatology wrote that the companies had not disclosed Phase 3 efficacy estimates
contradictions.counterexample: Practical Dermatology's actual language was more specific: 'The companies did not disclose hazard ratios, absolute event rates, P values, or other phase 3 efficacy estimates in the topline announcement.' The draft's paraphrase is accurate but understates the precision of what Practical Dermatology said, which included the specific enumeration the draft attributes to MLQ News.
contradictions.fix: Credit Practical Dermatology with the full enumeration — hazard ratios, absolute event rates, and P values — rather than the shorter paraphrase, and remove the same credit from MLQ News.

contradictions.quote: Two specialist outlets touched it [the stage IIB/IIC population difference], and they disagree. Morning Glory Sciences: the Phase 2b population was stage IIIB–IV, the Phase 3 adds node-negative disease... Pharmacy Times makes the opposite case.
contradictions.counterexample: This framing is broadly accurate, but the draft presents these as the only two outlets to raise the population difference. KOL Pulse also noted that KEYNOTE-942 enrolled 'stage III/IV melanoma' while INTerpath-001 enrolled stage IIB–IV, and Morning Glory Sciences' argument about absolute benefit in the lower-risk population is more fully developed than the draft conveys — it explicitly states that the Phase 3 hazard ratios have not been disclosed and therefore the comparison cannot be made at all, which is a methodological point rather than merely a clinical one.
contradictions.fix: Note that KOL Pulse also flagged the population difference, and clarify that Morning Glory Sciences' primary argument is methodological (the figures cannot be compared because Phase 3 numbers are absent) rather than purely clinical.

coverage.what_this_piece_can_add: No outlet found — including the most careful specialist coverage — discussed the OS interval's actual width (0.165–1.345) and what it means arithmetically, the descriptive-only status of the five-year KEYNOTE-942 analyses and why that matters for interpreting the interval clearing 1.0, the one-sided versus two-sided p-value distinction and the trial's own prespecified alpha of 0.10, the investigator-assessed endpoint detail in the Phase 3 and how blinding partially but not fully addresses it, or the absolute RFS percentage rates alongside the hazard ratios. These are the layers the draft uniquely adds beneath even the most careful reporting.
